summary: The stock Lua observer separates production and rally reads. Recoil GetUnitCommands on a factory reads newUnitCommands (rally), whereas GetFactoryCommands reads commandQue (production). The observed stock tuple contains domain, command ID, options, native tag and float parameters; timeout is unavailable and must not be invented. The selected HighBar stock FactoryProduce arm admits count one, checks current actor/build eligibility and stock queue policy, and sends options0: SHIFT would multiply stock factory production by five, while ordinary append is already the default. This differs from ordinary unit-order append and from the optional custom atomic replacement contract. Source/control qualification does not prove a loaded stock Count1 effect.
title: Stock production and rally queues require different APIs and option semantics
